subject: [Action Required] AZ service degradation — customer impact & ops/exec plan
messages:
From: Tim Girard <tim.girard@skylineanalytics.com>
To: Alex Martinez <alex_martinez@redwood.ai>
Cc: ingestops@skylineanalytics.com
Date: Sat, 10 Apr 2027 15:02:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Sudden latency + 5xx spike impacting Skyline pipelines

Alex —

We started seeing elevated tail latency and a 3-4% 5xx rate across our realtime ingest between ~14:45-15:30 UTC. Throughput dropped by about 25% and retries kicked in for several of our critical pipelines; customers are already reporting delayed dashboards. Attached a small sample from our side (traffic_snapshot.csv) showing the error bursts correlated to requests to your us-west-2 endpoint.

Can you confirm whether this is a regional issue? We need an ETA for mitigation and whether you can route us to another region while you investigate. This is impacting revenue reporting for some of our customers — we need an immediate escalation.

Thanks,
Tim
Tim Girard
Head of Platform Reliability, Skyline Analytics

From: Alex Martinez <alex_martinez@redwood.ai>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Sean Gallagher <sean_gallagher@redwood.ai>, Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.ai>
Cc: Tim Girard <tim.girard@skylineanalytics.com>
Date: Sat, 10 Apr 2027 15:18:00 -0700
Subject: Fwd: Sudden latency + 5xx spike impacting Skyline pipelines — urgent ops/exec

Team — escalating: Skyline (priority customer) reporting a region-level degradation impacting throughput and error rates against the us-west-2 AZs. Customer included trace sample and is requesting cross-region routing/failover.

Immediate asks:
- Marissa: can ops confirm whether this is an AZ-specific hardware/network event vs. degraded service due to executor/KV cache saturation? Trace suggests spikes concentrated to a subset of hosts.
- Sean: please prepare the executive brief (one-page) for CSM and Execs with options on credit/comp and expected ETA for failover window.
- Grace: coordinate with capacity/routing to pre-authorize a controlled cross-region shift (to us-west-1) and a fallback timeline. We should not do a full blanket failover without customer consent, but need a plan to route Skyline traffic if we cannot restore within 30m.

I will reply to Tim with an initial acknowledgement and list of actions.

— Alex
Alex Martinez
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
To: Alex Martinez <alex_martinez@redwood.ai>, Sean Gallagher <sean_gallagher@redwood.ai>, Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.ai>
Cc: Tim Girard <tim.girard@skylineanalytics.com>
Date: Sat, 10 Apr 2027 15:34:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Fwd: Sudden latency + 5xx spike impacting Skyline pipelines — ops update

Short operational update (investigation thread SUP-3421):
- Evidence points to a degraded network interface on a subset of hosts behind the us-west-2a ingress pool. Packet loss and increased retry between proxies and the serving runtime are causing request timeouts and secondary overload.
- Mitigation actions taken: isolated and drained 6 suspect hosts, increased request retries on the Skyline route to 4 with longer backoff, and enabled prefix cache bypass for affected tenants to reduce cache thrashing.
- We are preparing a controlled traffic migration plan to fail Skyline traffic to us-west-1 (readiness check OK) — estimated 20 minutes to complete validation and switch routing policies if agreed.

Attachments: kpi_sla_summary_20270410.png (customer-visible latency/5xx chart), incident_timeline_az_notes.txt (ops notes).

Prep notes for execs: impact window started ~2027-04-10T14:45Z; current mitigation is partial — we are seeing reduced 5xx but latency still elevated by ~80ms p50-to-p95. If degradation persists beyond 30 minutes, recommend scheduling the traffic migration.

— Marissa
Marissa Cole
Director, Runtime Operations, Redwood Inference

Date: Sun, 11 Apr 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Sudden latency + 5xx spike impacting Skyline pipelines — summary & next steps

Tim —

Apologies again for the disruption this morning. Quick summary of what we did and next steps: 

What we saw:
- Short burst of elevated 5xx (peak ~3.8%) and a 20–30% drop in throughput to Skyline tenants between ~14:45–15:25 UTC.

What we did immediately:
- Ops isolated and drained 6 suspect hosts in us-west-2a and applied a cache bypass for affected prefixes (reduced 5xx rate).
- We prepared a controlled cross-region migration to us-west-1; we did not move traffic without your consent.
- Increased retries and longer backoff on your route to reduce client-side immediate failures.

Recommended next steps (we propose):
1) If you approve, we can execute the controlled migration to us-west-1 within the next 20 minutes; otherwise we will continue targeted host remediation.
2) Post-incident: root-cause follow-up with packet captures and a permanent routing policy update to reduce blast radius for single-AZ network issues.
3) Sean will follow up on SLR credit and an executive note for your leadership.

We're deeply sorry for the impact. If you'd like, Marissa and I can join a quick call now to run through the technical details and the migration plan.

Best,
Alex Martinez
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
